findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Observed that the sanitizing solution (quaternary ammonium) in the sanitizer buckets was too low to effectively sanitize food-contact surfaces (100ppm). 
* The sanitizing solution is sourced from the triple sink sanitizing hose. The solution from the hose was at the lowest concentration that still effectively sanitizes (200ppm for quaternary ammonium). Because sanitizer can evaporate and deactivate over time, that indicates that the sanitizer buckets cannot maintain effective sanitizing concentration, as they were less than 1 hour old and already at a too low concentration.
* Inspector also observed that the water from the hose is hot, measuring at 124 F on a probe thermometer. Quaternary ammonium solutions should be used at room temperature water (75 F) per manufacturers instructions, as high temperatures can inactivate the sanitizer. Cold water is available at all facility faucets otherwise.
CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and will contact maintenance about the sanitizer hose temperature issue. PIC will cease using the sanitizing hose to fill sanitizer buckets until it is again providing proper concentrations for quaternary ammonium (200-400ppm). PIC remade the sanitizer buckets, this time using available bleach (Chlorine, effective concentration is 50-200ppm), which tested at 100ppm and 150ppm using facility’s test strips.
* PIC has quaternary ammonium tablets for the triple sink, and has sufficient test strips to check concentrations. 
* Most dishes are sanitized using the stationary rack dish machine (heat), which reaches effective sanitizing temperatures of 165 F.
Ensure sanitizing solutions are at safe and effective sanitizing concentrations for food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The shelving in the dry storage is observed to have an accumulation of soil on the metal racks. Ensure the shelving units are pulled out and thoroughly cleaned and sanitized. Ensure the shelving units are cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: Near the dish machine, blue anchors were observed to be in the wall with apparent holes present. These anchors need to be removed and the holes need to be sealed with caulking. Ensure the wall is repaired to make it smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed x5 dented cans stocked in on the rolling rack in the dry storage area. Cans were removed by inspector and immediately marked do not use and separated for return/disposal. Facility policy is to immediately return for credit but operator had an employee help stock cans who was not aware of the policy at the time. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. Ensure that all staff helping stock cans are aware that all dented cans must be removed prior to stocking in. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Some soil and debris was observed under the shelving near the back door. Ensure that the facility is cleaned often enough to prevent such accumulations from occurring. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a wet mop being stored in the bottom of a mop bucket instead of hanging in a manner which facilitates drying. Ensure that mops are either sitting in the top portion of the mop bucket or hanging inverted to prevent contamination, microbial growth and/or pests. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.
